---
title: Sweep
description: Reactive scope wrapper for automatic cleanup management with Charm and Vide integration
---

import { Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

Sweep is a reactive scope wrapper that combines Janitor's cleanup capabilities with Charm's effect system. It manages object lifecycles automatically within reactive scopes, making it the preferred cleanup solution for UI code over raw Janitor.

Sweep tracks a stack of active scopes, allowing nested cleanup registration without passing janitor instances around.

## Usage

### Basic Root Scope

```lua
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local Sweep = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Sweep)

-- Create a root scope with automatic cleanup
local cleanup, janitor = Sweep.root(function(j)
    -- Everything added to j is cleaned up when scope ends
    local connection = game:GetService('RunService').RenderStepped:Connect(function()
        print('Tick')
    end)
    j:Add(connection)
    
    -- Cloned instances are tracked
    local gui = Sweep.clone(ReplicatedStorage.Assets.MyGui)
    gui.Parent = LocalPlayer.PlayerGui
end)

-- Cleanup everything
cleanup()
```

### Effect Root with Charm

```lua
local Sweep = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Sweep)
local Charm = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Charm)

local isOpen = Charm.atom(false)

-- Reactive scope that rebuilds when dependencies change
Sweep.effect_root(function(initial, janitor)
    if not isOpen() then
        return -- Scope cleans up when isOpen becomes false
    end
    
    -- Setup UI that exists only while isOpen is true
    local gui = Sweep.clone(ReplicatedStorage.Assets.Popup)
    gui.Parent = LocalPlayer.PlayerGui
    
    -- Track internal reactive updates
    Sweep.effect(function()
        gui.Title.Text = titleAtom()
    end)
end)
```

### Cleanup and Clone Helpers

```lua
local Sweep = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Sweep)

Sweep.root(function(j)
    -- Clone and auto-track a prefab
    local button = Sweep.clone(ReplicatedStorage.Assets.Button)
    button.Parent = someFrame
    
    -- Manually track any object
    local tween = TweenService:Create(button, TweenInfo.new(0.3), {Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)})
    Sweep.clean(tween, 'Destroy')
    
    -- Track effects that re-run on atom changes
    Sweep.effect(function()
        local count = itemCount()
        button.Badge.Text = tostring(count)
        button.Badge.Visible = count > 0
    end)
end)
```

### Async and Spawn

```lua
local Sweep = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Sweep)

Sweep.root(function(j)
    -- Defer cleanup-tracked async work
    Sweep.async(function()
        local result = fetchData()
        -- Process result - automatically cleaned up
    end)
    
    -- Spawn with cleanup tracking
    Sweep.spawn(function()
        for i = 1, 10 do
            print(i)
            task.wait(1)
        end
    end)
end)
```

## API Reference

### root

```lua
function Sweep.root(callback: (janitor: Janitor) -> ()): (Cleanup, Janitor)
```

Creates a new cleanup scope. Everything added inside the callback is cleaned up when the returned function is called.

| Return | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `cleanup` | `() -> ()` | Function to destroy all tracked objects |
| `janitor` | `Janitor` | The underlying janitor instance |

### effect_root

```lua
function Sweep.effect_root(callback: (initial: boolean, janitor: Janitor) -> ())
```

Creates a reactive root scope tied to a Charm effect. The callback re-runs when any tracked atom changes, automatically cleaning up previous scope contents.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `initial` | `boolean` | `true` on first run, `false` on subsequent re-runs |
| `janitor` | `Janitor` | Cleanup bucket for this effect iteration |

### effect

```lua
function Sweep.effect(callback: () -> ())
```

Registers a Charm effect within the current Sweep scope. Automatically cleaned up when the scope ends.

### clean

```lua
function Sweep.clean(object: OBJ, methodName: BooleanOrString?): OBJ
```

Tracks an object for cleanup within the current scope. Returns the object for chaining.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `object` | `Instance \| Function \| thread \| RBXScriptConnection \| Tween` | Object to track |
| `methodName` | `boolean \| string?` | Cleanup method or `true` for `:Destroy()` |

### clone

```lua
function Sweep.clone(object: OBJ): OBJ
```

Clones an instance and automatically tracks it for cleanup. Returns the clone.

### cleanup

```lua
function Sweep.cleanup(object, methodName, index): Untrack
```

Low-level cleanup registration with optional index for manual removal.

| Return | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `untrack` | `() -> ()` | Function to remove from cleanup without cleaning |

### async

```lua
function Sweep.async(callback: (...) -> (), ...): Untrack
```

Defers callback execution via `task.defer` with automatic cleanup tracking.

### spawn

```lua
function Sweep.spawn(callback: (...) -> (), ...): Untrack
```

Spawns callback via `task.spawn` with automatic cleanup tracking.

## Why Sweep Over Janitor?

| Use Case | Solution |
|----------|----------|
| Imperative cleanup (systems, services) | Use Janitor directly |
| Reactive UI with Charm/Vide | Use Sweep |
| Effects that rebuild on state change | Use `Sweep.effect_root` |
| Simple scope without reactivity | Use `Sweep.root` |

Sweep eliminates the need to pass janitor instances through component hierarchies. The internal stack tracks the active scope automatically.

## Best Practices

- **Always use `Sweep.effect_root` for UI lifecycles** — automatically handles cleanup when UI unmounts
- **Use `Sweep.clone` over `instance:Clone()`** — ensures cleanup is tracked
- **Nest `Sweep.effect` inside roots** — child effects are cleaned up when parent re-runs
- **Don't yield in root callbacks** — use `Sweep.async` or `Sweep.spawn` instead
- **Prefer over raw Janitor for UI** — less boilerplate, automatic scope management
- **Root scopes are stack-based** — avoid deeply nested roots to prevent stack confusion
